bills.summary: Lets the Union postpone debts and cut interest for states and cities hit by declared calamities.
Creates the IBS management committee and rules for the new consumption tax.
Creates a National Day for Climate Action.
Sets principles for guaranteeing children's right to nature.
Reserves 30% of federal civil-service jobs for Black, Indigenous and quilombola candidates.
Changes the Chamber's rules on precautionary suspension of a deputy's mandate.
Approves amendments to the international convention on safety of life at sea.
Approves a Brazil–Colombia treaty against double taxation.
Creates a social-infrastructure investment fund and lets FDNE operators renegotiate debts.
Lets spending on federal university hospitals count toward the constitutional minimum for health.
Creates the national policy on critical and strategic minerals.
Lets cooperatives receive money from the Northeast Development Fund.
Adds education for responding to climate disasters to national laws.
Allows postponing rural-credit payments in areas under a declared calamity.
Requires electronic monitoring of aggressors in domestic-violence cases.
Creates a national campaign for conscious use of digital technology.
Specifies uses of the prison and public-security funds.
Creates the Propag programme to renegotiate states' debts with the Union.
Limits municipal payment of court-ordered debts and opens a new instalment plan for municipal pension debts.
Sets a transition for the payroll-tax substitution and the Cofins-Importação surcharge.
Approves a protocol to the Brazil–China double-taxation agreement.
Approves a Brazil–Croatia education cooperation agreement.
Changes simplified taxation of international postal remittances and the Mover programme.
Increases the state's capacity to respond to wildfires and similar disasters.
Changes the tax treatment of credit losses at financial institutions.
Changes the law creating the state air-navigation company NAV Brasil.
Includes vicarious violence in the Maria da Penha Law.
Approves a Brazil–China protocol on the CBERS-6 satellite.
Lets Simples Nacional small firms claim credit for tax residue returned in the production chain.
Opens an extraordinary credit for several ministries.
Sets rules for interfederal cooperation against transnational organised crime.
Includes student-assistance policies among priorities for the Social Fund.
Sets rules for proposing and executing parliamentary budget amendments.
Creates a National Axé Music Day.
Makes the Pronampe small-business credit programme permanent.
Bars condominium rules that restrict renting commercial units to political parties.
Ratifies property registries from sales and concessions of public land in border strips.
Changes agricultural policy, social-assistance and Bolsa Família rules as part of the 2024 spending-cut package.

votes.why: Yes grants federal debt relief to states and cities.
Yes allows state-backed postponement of rural-credit payments.
Yes gives banks tax relief on credit losses.
Yes gives small firms tax-credit relief.
Yes consolidates private property titles over former public land.
Senate version of the same measure.
Yes approves part of a spending-cut package on social programmes.
